newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Nippecraft shareholder sells 64 pct stake.
newsitem.headline: Nippecraft shareholder sells 64 pct stake.

text.p: Stationary maker Nippecraft said on Friday major shareholder St Kilda Investments (SKI) has sold 64 percent of its stake in the company for Singapore $44.8 million.

It said in a statement SKI accepted an unconditional offer from APP Printing (Holding) Pte Ltd (APH) to buy its entire shareholding of 128,000 shares in Nippecraft for $44.8 million, or S$0.35 a share.
APH is an investment company owned by Asia Pulp & Paper Company Ltd, controlled by Indonesian conglomerate Sinar Mas.

APH will subscribe for 32 million rights shares representing its entitlement under the proposed renounceable rights issue of 50 million new shares at S$0.28 per share announced by the company on December 24.

The terms of the rights issue will remain unchanged and DBS Bank has confirmed that it remains prepared to continue to underwrite the remaining 18 million rights shares at S$0.28, the Nippecraft statement said.
It said the company had asked Stock Exchange of Singapore to resume trading of its shares on Friday. Trading was suspended on Monday pending the negotiations, it said.
Nippecraft shares led the actives in early trade Friday, easing to a low of S$0.56. It was last traded at S$0.67 a share.
On Thursday, Nippecraft said it expected to incur a loss of $11.9 million in its current financial year ending March 31.
